name: Bothriochloa

project_scope.note: The stale Texas B. laguroides source concept is not a fourth learner species. Current project taxonomy represents the native silver bluestem concept as B. torreyana; species-lane reconciliation remains authoritative.

recognition.where_to_look_first: Check the stem nodes first, then the architecture of the seedhead. In the project set, nodal hair and the number/length/arrangement of rames split the three species quickly.
priority: many short rames versus a few long fingerlike branches
contracted cottony head versus broad fanlike head
awn and spikelet detail for confirmation

quick_split: B. barbinodis — conspicuous dense beard of hairs around the nodes; broader fanlike silvery panicle.
B. ischaemum — smooth nodes; loose terminal head with about 3–8 long fingerlike branches; introduced KR bluestem concept.
B. torreyana — smooth pale nodes; dense silver-white cottony contracted panicle made of many short fuzzy rames.
comparison_lesson.close_family_tie: Schizachyrium scoparium branches its upper culm into many short terminal fuzzy racemes rather than concentrating the seedhead into the Bothriochloa patterns above.

visual_needs: B. barbinodis closeup showing the dense nodal beard and a whole fanlike seedhead in the same lesson
B. ischaemum whole seedhead showing the 3–8 long fingerlike branches plus a smooth node closeup
